title: Refined phone model rendering and taps verified
summary: Replaced boxy wireframe-like rendering with a rounded phone enclosure, glass display, camera lenses, hardware details and a refined mobile viewer.

changes.detail: Rounded 3D extrusions, face visibility culling, layered lens optics, continuous metal frame, side buttons, port, speaker grilles, screen wallpaper, app tiles, clock and glass reflection.
Replaced average polygon-depth sorting that hid front-screen details. Centered and separated the display and chassis in the opened view; removed full-model selection wireframes.

Larger phone framing, studio-gradient background, compact segmented controls and rounded topic chips. Tapping a part or named topic brings its lesson into view. Existing lessons and saved progress preserved.
The new camera hit-test exposed a glass-reflection overlay intercepting taps. Decorative reflection faces now pass through hit testing; all three language cases pass.

validation.name: Phone lab regression tests
validation.detail: Four tests passed after the reflection correction, including actual front camera icon hit testing, front/back geometry, rotation, all topics, quiz feedback and progress in English/French/Arabic.

validation.name: TypeScript and lint
validation.detail: App typecheck and focused renderer/document ESLint passed after final edits.

validation.name: History retention
validation.detail: Six history tests passed; all previous reports are retained.

validation.name: Direct model visual inspection
validation.detail: Canvas draw commands replayed to SVG and rendered to PNG. Front, rear and separated views inspected; corrected screen occlusion and opened-view clipping. These artifacts are model renders, not browser screenshots.

validation.name: Live app and physical device
validation.detail: Live browser layout and native WebView were not visually tested. The phone remains a stylized educational model, not a model-specific photorealistic teardown. No deployment.
